content.introduction: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) holds eight regularly scheduled meetings per year to review economic and financial conditions, determine the appropriate stance of monetary policy, and assess risks to its long-term goals. Before each meeting, the FOMC Secretariat distributes memos covering economic, financial, and monetary issues. At the meeting, staff officers present reports, and committee members discuss economic and monetary policy. The meeting typically ends with a formal vote on policy actions, which are released to the public at 2:00 p.m. (ET), followed by a press conference by Fed Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. (ET).
body:
First off, Chair Powell works with the FOMC Secretariat, currently Joshua Gallin, to produce an agenda for the Committee meeting. It includes standard topics such as reports on open market operations, the economic situation, and monetary policy alternatives, as well as any special items. Special items for the May meeting could plausibly include an update on developments in the banking sector as well as a report on the effects of a potential U.S. default. The Secretariat then sends the finished [...] Ahead of each meeting, the Secretariat also distributes memos to the FOMC participants. These memos generally cover the economic, financial, and monetary issues as described by the Fed Board staff. [...] At last, the meeting normally ends around 12:00 p.m. (ET) with each FOMC member formally voting to approve the policy action and statement.

The statement gets released to the public at 2:00 p.m. (ET) and Fed Chair Powell then gives a press conference at 2:30 p.m. (ET) and the market fun ensues.

Before each regularly scheduled meeting of the FOMC, System staff prepare written reports on past and prospective economic and financial developments that are sent to committee members and to nonmember Reserve Bank presidents. Reports prepared by the manager of the System Open Market Account on operations in the domestic open market and in foreign currencies since the last regular meeting are also distributed. At the meeting itself, staff officers present oral reports on the current and [...] By law, the FOMC must meet at least four times each year in Washington, D.C. Since 1981, eight regularly scheduled meetings have been held each year at intervals of five to eight weeks. If circumstances require consultation or consideration of an action between these regular meetings, members may be called on to participate in a special meeting or a telephone conference, or to vote on a proposed action by proxy. At each regularly scheduled meeting, the committee votes on the policy to be [...] After these reports, the committee members and other Reserve Bank presidents turn to policy. Typically, each participant expresses their own views on the state of the economy and prospects for the future and on the appropriate direction for monetary policy. Then each makes a more explicit recommendation on policy for the coming intermeeting period (and for the longer run, if under consideration).

The FOMC holds eight regularly scheduled meetings per year. At these meetings, the Committee reviews economic and financial conditions, determines the appropriate stance of monetary policy, and assesses the risks to its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth.

For more information about the FOMC and monetary policy, see the "Monetary Policy" section of The Fed Explained: What the Central Bank Does. FOMC Rules and Authorizations are available online.
